spoken: Before we get to that European nightmare, Real Madrid are pursuing eighty million euros from six Premier League clubs. Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, and Tottenham have all been asked to pay their share of the costs from that failed Super League.

They signed the papers, so they should pay their share! But look at the pitch, Dhruv. Martin Demichelis brings RB Leipzig to the Bernabeu late tonight, and they are struggling. Leipzig sit twenty-first in the Champions League phase and have lost five of their last six away matches. Madrid have won nine of their last eleven games. This should be routine, right?

On paper, yes, but the squad is stretched. Ferland Mendy is listed as absent, while Raul Asencio and Rodrygo are completely ruled out. The positive news is that Antonio Rudiger and Denzel Dumfries are expected back in the starting line-up. Madrid already won both their opening matches, including that comeback in Rome from 3-1 down with three goals in the final eight minutes.

That Rome night was special. And Thibaut Courtois spoke up on DAZN ahead of the Ballon d'Or in London next Monday. He stated that individually nobody has been better than Kylian Mbappe. He acknowledged Lamine Yamal has trophies with Spain, but on individual merit alone, Mbappe should take it.

Courtois raised the dilemma between individual brilliance and collective silverware. Now, switching to cricket, India have landed in Christchurch for five T20 matches against New Zealand. Mitchell Santner has already admitted that fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will be hard to stop if he plays, and New Zealand have done research to prepare for him.
Will Bhuvi get straight into the starting eleven, though? Santner seems genuinely worried about Bhuvneshwar Kumar in swinging conditions.

Santner warned that Bhuvneshwar will love the movement in New Zealand. Shreyas Iyer also pointed out that the bowling attack lacked experience after the IPL, especially with Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya out injured. Youngsters like Mayank Yadav, Prince Yadav, and Gurnoor Brar leaked runs on flat tracks, whereas Bhuvneshwar brings ninety wickets from eighty-eight T20 internationals and back-to-back IPL titles with RCB. He took twenty-eight wickets in 2026 alone.
Having Bhuvi back with the new ball changes everything. Shifting to Formula One, can you actually believe what Christian Horner admitted in his book?

It is quite an admission in Drive. Horner revealed he deliberately pressured Michael Masi during the safety car at Abu Dhabi in 2021. When Nicholas Latifi crashed, Hamilton was leading, and five lapped cars sat between Lewis and a freshly pitted Max Verstappen. Horner admitted his heart sank because overtaking all five cars in one lap was impossible, so he told Masi to get those lapped cars out of the way.

Max himself is focused on Austin, though he watched the endurance race at the Circuit of the Americas and sounded terrified of the track surface. He joked that it was so bumpy he might need to order a new spine and look like RoboCop after the weekend! Red Bull arrive as favourites after two wins, a sprint win, and a second place across the last three rounds, but Max is taking it race by race.

A sensible mindset given how different the tracks are. In tennis, John McEnroe appeared on television in Madrid and labeled Carlos Alcaraz the best thing to happen to the sport in ten years. He also noted how lucky everyone is to have him back from that wrist injury. John Isner also spoke about Alcaraz taking a wildcard into Vienna next week. Isner believes Carlos is fresh after his break and determined to prove he remains the world's best ahead of the ATP Finals in Turin, with Jannik Sinner absent.
Now for Rival Watch. Paris Saint-Germain four, Barcelona two! Did anyone see that defensive collapse coming in Paris?
Barcelona entered the game with five straight wins, but Paris dismantled them in the second half.

Dismantled is an understatement! Desire Doue opened the scoring from a Joao Neves pass before the break. Xavi Espart leveled for Barcelona from a Fermin Lopez assist. Then Lucas Hernandez scored a header from another Doue cross. Lamine Yamal dragged Barcelona level at two-all in the seventy-ninth minute, and they celebrated like they had stolen a point. Two minutes later, Vitinha struck. Five minutes after that, Fabian Ruiz scored from an Achraf Hakimi assist to seal it 4-2. Absolutely ragged defending!

A terrible result for them ahead of the weekend. Over in Basel, Novak Djokovic accepted a wildcard for the Swiss Indoors, returning there for the first time since his 2010 final loss to Roger Federer. Andy Roddick noted that with the Six Kings Slam delayed until December, Djokovic needs match rhythm in Basel and Paris to prepare for the Australian Open.

Is Draymond getting carried away again with the young guys? On his show, Draymond Green anointed fourteenth draft pick Yaxel Lendeborg as the next face of the Golden State Warriors and backed him for Rookie of the Year, with Kristaps Porzingis out indefinitely.

Draymond said similar things about James Wiseman and Jonathan Kuminga, so take it with a pinch of salt. In football, Erik ten Hag told The Athletic that Cristiano Ronaldo let him and the team down back in 2022 when Ronaldo refused to come on against Tottenham.
Ten Hag is still explaining that fallout four years on. What is this new rule in Formula One?

The FIA added a strict operational regulation to shut a budget cap loophole. Teams can no longer use separate engineering divisions, such as Red Bull Advanced Technologies or Mercedes Applied Sciences, to secretly develop their cars. Also in Austin, Cadillac are running a cowboy-themed livery, with Colton Herta driving Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez's car in opening practice.

Around the grounds. Animal rights group PETA has written to Crystal Palace demanding they retire their live bald eagle mascot, Phoenix. PETA argued that the loud, boisterous stadium environment at Selhurst Park causes severe distress and panic for birds.

spoken: Four-one! Real Madrid made it look so easy in the Champions League last night.
They carried four wins from five into it, and Bernardo Silva set things off in the forty-third minute.
Then Arda Guler scored off a Kylian Mbappe assist in the fifty-second. Guler even joked after the match that he stole Mbappe's goal because he knew Mbappe would score another anyway!

And Mbappe did score in the eighty-third, set up by Yan Diomande. Tidiam Gomis got one back for Leipzig two minutes later, but Diomande smashed a volley from Brahim Diaz in the eighty-seventh to complete the four-one win.
Even the Leipzig manager admitted Madrid's quality is hard to match and backed them to win La Liga and the Champions League!
Did you see what is happening with Trent Alexander-Arnold?

It is crazy! He wanted to win the Ballon d'Or here, but he has become a bit-part player. Jose Mourinho is playing midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back ahead of him and summer signing Denzel Dumfries. Now Xabi Alonso has approved Chelsea moving for Alexander-Arnold.

Meanwhile, Jarell Quansah dodged questions about his future before Bayer Leverkusen played OFI Crete. Liverpool have a seventy million euro buy-back clause active in 2027, but Arsenal and Real Madrid are tracking him too.
Jurgen Klopp weighed in on El Clasico! He admitted he disliked Madrid stars historically, but says he will watch the match and keep an eye on German forward Karim Adeyemi.
Mourinho also defended Vinicius Junior recently, stating he is satisfied with his performance.
What is the update on India's tour of New Zealand?

The team arrived jetlagged, but Virtual Eye's 'Sonic' edge-detection technology has been approved for the DRS starting in Christchurch. Also, Pakistan pulled out of the International Masters Cricket World Cup after PCB chief Mohsin Naqvi refused permission for their veterans to travel to India.
Over to Formula 1 in Austin! Max Verstappen is aiming for three wins in a row after Sepang and Singapore!

Verstappen sits fourth on two hundred and twenty-one points, trailing leader Kimi Antonelli by one hundred and nineteen points. Off the track, Christian Horner's new book 'Drive' caused friction, with Helmut Marko calling his statements a collection of untruths. And Ferrari's Fred Vasseur dismissed claims that Red Bull are the team to beat.

In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz is preparing for the Vienna Open by practicing with a top fifty player in Murcia. His former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero hit back at critics defending Alexander Zverev's year-end number one ranking and two Grand Slams.
Not a great opening night for Golden State.
It was brutal! The Lakers won one hundred and twenty-seven to one hundred and five. Steph Curry scored sixteen of our first twenty-one points, but finished with twenty-three in twenty-one minutes.

Luka Doncic dropped twenty-eight, Walker Kessler had twenty-six points and nine rebounds, and Austin Reaves scored twenty-three. The Lakers led by thirty-four by the end of the third quarter. Yaxel Lendeborg even told Doncic he sucks during the game.
And the Warriors are exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis while he deals with auto-immune condition POTS. That is tough news.

In tennis, Novak Djokovic took a late wildcard for Basel to chase ATP Finals qualification. He trails Alex de Minaur by forty points. Elsewhere, a court in Pristina sentenced Milorad Djokovic to ten years in prison for war crimes committed in Ozdrim in 1999.
In football, Harry Kane scored in his tenth straight Champions League game for Bayern against Arsenal. He is just one away from Cristiano Ronaldo's record of eleven set in 2017.
For the US Grand Prix, the FIA approved two Straight Mode active aero zones. Ferrari also revealed a blueprint-inspired special livery with HP.
Did you see Como beat Manchester United four-one in the Champions League?
A heavy loss for United. And cricket legend Jimmy Anderson is expected to retire at forty-four after Lancashire decided against renewing his contract.

spoken: We begin in Spain. A huge Clasico is coming on Sunday, with an expected global audience topping 600 million, easily beating the IPL final's 400 million. But the ugly headlines off the pitch are dominating everything.

It is appalling. Javier Tebas went on X and compared Real Madrid's communication methods to Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister! Real Madrid immediately called for Tebas to resign. How does La Liga let their president get away with that?

He might not get away with it. Spain's National Sports Council has referred the sixty-four-year-old to the Administrative Court for Sport to see if it violates the 1990 Sports Law regarding sporting dignity and decorum. On the pitch, Jose Mourinho is taking Madrid to Spotify Camp Nou, returning to the ground where he worked decades ago.
The atmosphere is going to be electric. Have you seen what Max has been saying about the track in Austin?

Both he and Lando Norris are sounding the alarm over the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas. Even with resurfacing between turns nine and eleven, Verstappen called the surface out of control and unacceptable.
Max actually revealed his spine scans show the bottom end does not look great. Even with that beating, he was only less than a tenth off Charles Leclerc in opening practice.

Leclerc set the pace for Ferrari at 1:36.052, Norris was third, and track limit deletions caused chaos. Across to cricket, Harry Brook blasted a double century in Rawalpindi off just 114 balls with twenty-one fours and ten sixes, three balls faster than Shubman Gill against West Indies. Yet England lost as Sri Lanka chased 430. Does Brook's innings still count as historic for you?

A stunning knock, but Brook himself said it means nothing in a defeat. On a brighter note for India, Bhuvneshwar Kumar spoke about his comeback after four years away. He said having no expectations and staying present gave him patience and maturity.
And in tennis, Carlos Alcaraz has become the first player confirmed for the 2027 Queen's Club Championships, locking in grass-court preparation after injuries disrupted his summer.
Right, Golden State. How did we manage to throw that away?
A total fourth-quarter collapse. The Warriors led Memphis by twelve with just over three minutes left in their home opener at Chase Center, and then Memphis ripped off a 17-2 run to steal it 111-108.

Former Warrior Ty Jerome drops twenty-eight points on us! Cameron Boozer hits the go-ahead basket with nineteen point seven seconds left. Steph Curry answers with an unbelievable fadeaway three, only for the whistle to blow. An illegal screen called on Draymond Green!

Steve Kerr was furious, picked up a technical foul, and claimed there was flopping on illegal screen calls all night. Golden State sit 0-2, and Brandin Podziemski is now out against Phoenix to protect a lower back strain, right after scoring eighteen points against Memphis.
Just brutal breaks. What do you make of Daniil Medvedev taking aim at Novak Djokovic?

Medvedev insists there should be no wildcards for Djokovic if he misses the ATP Finals. Novak is eleventh in the race right now, though ninth place qualifies because Jannik Sinner withdrew. Do you agree with Medvedev on the Djokovic wildcard?
Rules are rules, Daniil has a point. Did you catch Cristiano Ronaldo celebrating his latest goal?

Against Al-Faisaly, João Félix whipped in a free kick, Ronaldo headed it, and it clearly deflected off defender Andrei Girotto. Opta classed it an own goal, but the Saudi Pro League gave it to Ronaldo as his 982nd career goal, complete with his Siuuu routine.
He will take anything towards a thousand. And Adrian Newey sounded surprisingly upbeat about Aston Martin.
Newey says team spirit at Silverstone is very strong, even if Honda are a little bit behind where he hoped.
Around the grounds. A shocking scoreline in the Europa League: Bournemouth blew AC Milan away 3-0.
Milan beaten by three goals! Nobody saw that coming.
And in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series, Sri Lanka pulled off the second-highest successful chase in ODI history, tracking down 430 to beat England by two wickets with just one ball to spare.

spoken: Two-nil up in New Zealand. Chasing one hundred and eighty-one, six down, and Tilak pulls off a proper late heist with one ball left. Brilliant.
Did you honestly think they were pulling that off with an over to spare?
I had my doubts! But everyone online is praising the Telugu brothers, Tilak and Nitish Kumar Reddy. They held their nerve completely.

New Zealand ended on one hundred and eighty for five, and India reached one hundred and eighty-one for six in nineteen point five overs. It puts India two-nil up with three to play. The third match is on Tuesday in Wellington.
And the Kiwis are already shuffling their pack.

Heavy rotation. Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry sit out the third T20I. Ferguson returns for games four and five in Auckland and Hamilton. Henry stays in Christchurch to prepare for the one-day squad on November second. Kyle Jamieson plays domestic cricket for Canterbury on October thirty-first before the one-dayers, while Blair Tickner joins the group in Wellington.
Arshdeep Singh, though. Two for thirty-three today, and that is thirty-eight T20 international wickets in 2026. A new Indian record in a calendar year!

He went past Bhuvneshwar Kumar's thirty-seven wickets from 2022. Arshdeep did it in twenty-six innings, whereas Bhuvneshwar took thirty-one. Only Josh Little with thirty-nine and Wanindu Hasaranga on thirty-eight are in that bracket.
Speaking of Bhuvi, did you see Ajinkya Rahane's all-time India Test eleven?

I did. He only picked players he shared a dressing room with. Vijay and Dhawan opening, Dravid at three, Tendulkar at four, Rahane at five, Dhoni at six as captain and keeper. Then Jadeja, Ashwin, Bhuvneshwar, Shami, and Ishant. No Virat Kohli. No Rohit Sharma.

Leaving out Virat and Rohit is a massive call! Meanwhile, Suryakumar Yadav was in Mumbai at the Andheri Sports Complex swinging a baseball bat. Three-on-three with retired major leaguers like Nick Swisher and Adrian Gonzalez. Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar, and Radha Yadav played too.
A charity crossover. Now, the big one tonight. El Clasico at Camp Nou.
I am terrified, Dhruv. Barcelona have won nine out of nine in the league, scored thirty-nine goals, and matched a fifty-year-old record after putting five past Betis. We are six points behind them.
Jose Mourinho walks back into Camp Nou for his first Clasico since his first stint ended in 2013. Can Madrid really hold them off without Vinicius?
That four-match ban hurts so much. The appeal failed, so Vinicius misses out after that Villarreal red card. Yan Diomande gets the nod on the left wing. We have to break their momentum.
In Austin, qualifying did not go to plan for Max Verstappen either. Kimi Antonelli snatched pole with a 1:34.035 in Q3. Verstappen starts second, just under two tenths behind.
Max was completely baffled. He clocked a 1:34.214, said he made no mistakes, but the car was sliding everywhere and then the wind picked up. Toto Wolff admitted Mercedes only expected third to fifth!
Isack Hadjar took third. But Verstappen has also been vocal about the track surface, revealing scans showed damage to his spinal discs from the severe bumps.
Is Verstappen's back genuinely that bad, Dhruv?
He is taking painkillers this weekend. Lewis Hamilton dismissed it, though, saying the bumps give the circuit character and everyone has to deal with them.
Carlos Alcaraz is heading indoors next. The Vienna Open main draw begins on Monday at the Wiener Stadthalle. Alexander Zverev is top seed, Alcaraz is second, alongside Medvedev and Mensik.
Alexander Blockx has withdrawn from that field.
Over in the NBA, Golden State are in serious trouble. Phoenix Suns 131, Warriors 122. We are zero and three!
That has not happened to the Warriors in nineteen years. It is the first zero and three start of Stephen Curry's career.

They were on the second night of a back-to-back, third game in four days. Steph rested with a sore right knee. Podziemski, Draymond, and Al Horford were all out with lower back issues. Devin Booker went wild for forty-three points, seventeen in the third quarter alone.
Luke Kennard sank three triples to seal it. Can the Warriors keep floating two-way guys into starting spots?

No chance. Seth Curry called it out on Threads after Graham Ike started at center against Memphis. Kristaps Porzingis signed that two-year, forty million dollar extension and is out indefinitely with health problems. Charles Bassey is out too. The front court is empty.
Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has certainly brought noise, picking up technical fouls in his first two games and pushing Ty Jerome on Friday.
He said he lost all respect for Luka Doncic because of complaining to referees. Bold words from a rookie saying Luka is not Michael Jordan!
Cristiano Ronaldo was on social media today marking Al Nassr's seventy-first anniversary since their founding in 1955.
Over one hundred and thirty goals since he joined in 2023. He called it seventy-one years of passion.
"He will take anything towards a thousand." You said it yesterday, Kylo. Well, today he is celebrating the club.
Fair point! Do you see Antonelli sealing the world championship tonight?
He must win the United States Grand Prix to take the title. If he does not win, the title fight rolls onto Mexico City.
Jeremy Clarkson caused outrage in the paddock, calling Franco Colapinto's ten-place grid drop a penalty for being Argentine. Colapinto's management called the comment unacceptable.

On the tennis courts, Tallon Griekspoor beat Francisco Cerundolo in three sets to make the European Open final, where he meets Jan-Lennard Struff, who edged Arthur Fils in a final-set tiebreak. In Almaty, Nikoloz Basilashvili knocked out Stefanos Tsitsipas in three sets, and Daniil Medvedev advanced after Alexander Bublik retired trailing 6-3.
Huge shock in the Premier League. Aston Villa took down Manchester City two-one!

And in cricket, Namibia stunned Ireland by thirty-one runs in Windhoek. Gerhard Erasmus hit a masterclass unbeaten one hundred and fifty-six off one hundred and twenty-five balls, lifted them to 321 for 6, and took the final two wickets to level the series one-all. Paul Stirling made seventy-seven for Ireland.

spoken: I am still floating! We went into Barcelona six points behind, under massive pressure, and pulled off a 2-1 victory! Mbappé opened it in the 41st minute, Raphinha equalised in the 61st, and then Mbappé again off Eduardo Camavinga's assist in the 87th minute!
Exactly when Jose Mourinho needed it. That cuts the gap at the top to three points.
Where does that leave us in the standings?
Barcelona stay top on 27 points. Atlético Madrid are second with 25, Real Madrid move to third with 24 points, and Real Betis are fourth on 20.
That changes the whole mood around Madrid!

Although former Madrid keeper Santi Canizares raised questions on COPE about the Mbappé and Vinicius Jr partnership. He argued their lack of defensive work leaves Bellingham working twice as much and leaves the team disconnected up front.
Canizares can say what he wants, Mbappé reached 100 goals for Real Madrid! In just 116 appearances!

He is the second-fastest to a hundred goals for Madrid in the 21st century, behind only Cristiano Ronaldo's 105 matches. Sixty-seven in La Liga, 25 in the Champions League, four in Copa del Rey, two in the Club World Cup, one in the UEFA Super Cup, and one in the Spanish Super Cup.
Unbelievable! But did you see Guti hitting out at Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or in London over Lamine Yamal and Mbappé? He called it orchestrated!
Kane scored 73 goals for club and country, so Thomas Tuchel certainly felt it was deserved. Even Virat Kohli congratulated Kane on X, praising his resilience and hard work.
Speaking of cricket, how about Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashing 100 in five overs?
That set a new world record for the fastest team hundred in men's T20Is. They equalled the fastest fifty in 2.2 overs and got the highest total in the first six overs.
Pure carnage at the top!
Out in Wellington, Daryl Mitchell hit a 52-ball 89 to push New Zealand to 198 for 3 in the third T20I. India's bowlers did well at the finish though, giving away just 52 runs in the last five overs.
Now, Formula 1 at Austin... Max Verstappen finished third from second on the grid behind winner Antonelli and Leclerc.
That P3 mathematically ends Max's title hopes. It ends a streak of 2,184 days where he was in contention for the world championship, going back to 2020.
Six years! Four titles in between! But the team radio failed him again!
He was furious. He joked they should start communicating in sign language because the Red Bull radio keeps dropping out.
And Isack Hadjar finished sixth after clutch troubles off the line and a bad engine map that limited his throttle.

In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz faces Karen Khachanov today in Vienna. He is also set to lead Spain's Davis Cup Finals team in Bologna alongside Rafael Jodar, Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, Marcel Granollers, and Pedro Martinez.
Who is in the Germany squad?
Alexander Zverev, Jan-Lennard Struff, Kevin Krawietz, and Tim Puetz. Ben Shelton mentioned recently that it was sad for tennis to have Alcaraz and Sinner miss so much of the year due to injuries.
Time for Rival Watch! Barcelona had nine wins from nine in the league, talking about running away with La Liga! Then Mourinho brings Real Madrid to town and hands them a 2-1 defeat on their own turf!
Raphinha scored, but Mbappé's double broke their perfect domestic start. A satisfying slip for them.
The Warriors finally got a win! 134-114 over Denver!

After three straight losses, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg exploded for 31 points and 12 rebounds. Steph Curry had a solid game, Al Horford added 11 off the bench hitting 3-for-3 from deep, and Golden State shot 54 percent from the field to avoid an 0-4 start. Nikola Jokic had 19 points before sitting out.
Did you hear about Alex Albon and Fernando Alonso clashing at Austin?
Alonso took a jab at the quality at the back of the grid after their Turn 11 collision. Albon replied that it was like watching a Mustang race a Mini at Goodwood.
And Toto Wolff spoke out on George Russell?
Yes, Wolff defended Russell, saying he is a champion who struggles when the car drops out of its operating window.
Any update on Jannik Sinner?

Sinner is returning at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh this December after his knee injury. Also, over 150 men's doubles players signed an open letter protesting the ATP's proposed draw and prize money cuts for 2028.
